Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

visitor noun

a guest who calls or stays

also visitors, house guest, guest (staying), caller, have visitors, have guests staying

classical

Sen. Ep. 64.1: hospitēs vēnisse
Ov. F. 5.502: hospitibus jānua nostra patet

hospes, hospitis m.

noun, third declension; feminine hospita, hospitae

guest, visitor

A guest who comes to the house, to call or to stay; at the table he is a convīva (see guest). The same word is the host (see host): the sentence shows which is meant.

Other words

  • salūtātor, salūtātōris m. — a caller who comes to pay his respects

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Q. Cic. Pet. 34; Mart. 1.71.18 (Lewis & Short)

    The Roman morning caller at a great man’s house, and later a courtier (Lewis & Short): a visit of courtesy, not a friend dropping in.

Examples

  • sī vespertīnus subitō tē oppresserit hospes

    if a visitor descends on you suddenly in the eveningHor. S. 2.4.17

  • et hospitibus jānua nostra patet

    and our door is open to visitorsOv. F. 5.502

  • hospes, hīc bene manēbis, hīc summum bonum voluptās est

    guest, you will be well off staying here; here the highest good is pleasureSen. Ep. 21.10

See also guest, host, visit, receive, invite, guest room, centre.

SourcesLewis & Short: hospes · Lewis & Short: salutator
